calls.head: Sheltered vs. Exposed
calls.body: The Rangers keep dangerous shots away, but the Ducks give up a lot of them. The Rangers are one of the league’s best for preventing dangerous shots, and Anaheim is near the bottom. The more dangerous chances should come at the Ducks’ net.
calls.call: The Rangers prevent dangerous shots better than the Ducks do.

calls.beyond: The Rangers usually get better looks than most teams, and Anaheim usually allows more dangerous shots than most teams. Even by those standards, this was a night of good looks: the Rangers’ shots at 5-on-5 had a 9.7% chance of scoring on the average shot, against their usual 6.6% (about 6.8% against Anaheim) and a league average of 6.3%. A team strays this far about once every 35 games.

surprises.head: Both teams played to type
surprises.body: Nothing in this game strayed far from how these two usually play: the shot share, the quality of chances, special teams, hitting, ice time and goaltending all landed inside their normal night-to-night range.

story.head: Bjorkstrand has two goals as the Rangers take down the Ducks
paras: Nick Jensen made his Ducks debut, after two seasons with the Senators. Sean Durzi struck first for the Rangers a little over a minute in, and J.T. Miller stretched the lead to 2-0 on the power play early in the second. Gabe Perreault and Oliver Bjorkstrand scored just under three minutes apart midway through the period to stretch the lead to 4-0. Bjorkstrand scored again early in the third to make it 5-0. Jensen got the Ducks on the board with just over a minute left, but by then the game was long gone. A.J. Greer scored his first goal for Anaheim with 33 seconds left to make it 5-2.

The Rangers had the better of the chances. Dylan Garand made 29 saves for the Rangers, and Ville Husso stopped 25 of 30 at the other end. The Rangers moved to 7-3-1, second in the Metropolitan, while the Ducks fell to 4-4-0, fifth in the Pacific.
